scope: single controlled fixed path; no PlayWorld score or SOTA claim

memory.method: bounded early-view pose KV retrieval; diagnostic, not paper reproduction
memory.pose_source: commanded poses, not reconstructed realized poses
memory.key_storage: canonical pre-RoPE BF16 keys; reapply spatial and virtual temporal RoPE on read

caveat: Commanded camera closure does not prove realized closure. Endpoint image similarity cannot establish world memory if the realized route fails.

visual_judge.prompt: Evaluate two anonymized world-model videos independently and then compare. Each was given the same image and fixed camera path. Commands by one-second chunk: ['WAIT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'LEFT', 'LEFT', 'LEFT', 'WAIT']. RIGHT and LEFT yaw 60 degrees per second; W moves forward. Commands are NOT proof that motion happened. Inspect actual frames. Assess whether each video realizes a turnaround and return to the starting viewpoint; whether persistent landmark identity, any sign text, geometry and spatial layout match on return; and whether there are sudden jumps, frozen motion or implausible transitions. Distinguish camera-control failures from forgetting. Do not reward a similar final building if reaching it required a reset. Do not invent unseen geometry. Return English JSON with keys A and B (each with realized_round_trip: yes|no|uncertain, starting_place_recovered: yes|no|uncertain, discontinuity: yes|no|uncertain, visual_evidence, failure_classification), preference: A|B|tie|neither, confidence: low|medium|high, and reasoning. This is a diagnostic comparison, not a benchmark score.

A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-9 hold the opening view: the Primemall building with its triangular dark roof, diamond-tiled orange facade, 'Primemall' sign and glass entrance. During RIGHT (about frames 10-50) the camera pans smoothly past the second orange building with the 'Drienmaell' sign and fountain pool, then the 'Primeseen' facade, and settles on a plaza with blue umbrellas and a sunken seating area behind glass railings. That plaza view holds steadily through the WAIT period (about frames 50-119), with only minor shimmer. During LEFT (frames 120-149) the pan reverses in the same order: plaza, Primeseen facade, Drienmaell building with fountain, then the original Primemall building. Around frames 140-145 (detail sample 7) the original building returns with the same triangular roof, tiled facade, 'Primemall' sign text, glass entrance and lamp posts, closely matching frame 0. The rotation then overshoots slightly. In the final frames (150-158) the original building sits at the right edge with only 'Prin' visible. A blue-trimmed storefront and glass stair railings appear on the left; these were not in the opening view but are plausible newly revealed areas. Motion blur appears at the pan onsets, but there are no hard cuts.
A.failure_classification: Minor camera-control imprecision. The return rotation overshoots the starting yaw, so the final framing is offset to the left. The scene is not forgotten: landmark identity, sign text and layout are preserved on return, and the reverse path is consistent with the outbound one.

B.visual_evidence: Frames 0-124 are essentially identical to Video A: the same opening Primemall view, the same rightward pan to the umbrella plaza, and the same stable hold. During LEFT the camera does rotate, but the scene does not retrace the outbound path. At about frames 121-125 the plaza blurs into a view where the sign reads 'Pinemall' or 'Prineml' and dark triangular roof elements merge with the plaza's pools and umbrellas. By frames 126-134 a triangular-roofed tiled building appears with only a faded '...emall' fragment, and blue umbrellas and pools sit directly in front of it, a layout that was never adjacent to the original building. The Drienmaell/fountain sequence seen on the way out is skipped. From about frame 130 onward a new glass building with a bright blue tiled band, a round logo and garbled 'Prim...' text dominates the view. The video ends (frames 140-158) on an unseen paved courtyard with a central planter strip, glass railings and zig-zag rooftops in the distance. The original Primemall facade, sign and entrance never reappear in their original framing.
B.failure_classification: Spatial forgetting and hallucination rather than camera-control failure. Yaw motion does occur, but the reverse pan generates a recombined and then entirely new scene. The return segment also contains implausible morphing transitions.

result.reasoning: The two videos are identical until the LEFT segment, so the comparison rests entirely on the return. Video A retraces the outbound sequence in reverse (plaza, Primeseen, Drienmaell with fountain, Primemall). It recovers the original landmark with consistent geometry and readable 'Primemall' signage, and its only flaw is a modest yaw overshoot at the end. Video B rotates but loses the scene. It blends the plaza into a distorted version of the triangular-roof building, skips the intermediate buildings, and ends on a hallucinated blue-signed building and courtyard that never appeared. A's error is a pose offset; B's is memory loss.
